title: Thu 12 Nov · evening check
summary:
[b]Today:[/b] UK Q3 GDP +0.7% in line (no GBP change), BoJ's Asada pushed back on fast hikes (yen +6 scenario less likely), Fed's Hammack and Goolsbee stayed hawkish, oil and gold softer.
[b]Tomorrow:[/b] Euro-area GDP 12:00 Bucharest · US PPI 15:30 · Fitch Germany / S&P Italy late.

USD.note: Hammack and Goolsbee hawkish; December hike ~91%; claims 200k vs 195k (medium, no score effect).

EUR.note: No new OAT–Bund reading since 142.4bp (10 Nov); euro-area GDP tomorrow 12:00 Bucharest.

GBP.note: UK Q3 GDP +0.7% q/q in line (Sept +0.2% vs 0.0%); not a clear beat. Dec BoE hike priced ~66–73%.

JPY.note: BoJ's Asada urged caution on the pace of hikes; Kihara: weak yen a problem. No fresh December pricing.

CHF.note: No new SNB item or Swiss data.

CAD.note: Brent ~$91.3, WTI ~$85.3 early Thursday; EIA figure not verified.

AUD.note: No verifiable RBA item or Australian release today.

NZD.note: No new item; dairy auction 17 Nov.

XAU.status: INVALIDATED by written rule (model still bullish)
XAU.note: Gold own score +7, or +4 if real yields keep rising; gold at its lowest since 4 Nov early Thursday.

[b]A Bank of Japan dove spoke up, and the yen's December hopes got a little quieter.[/b]
Board member Toichiro Asada, who voted against both of this year's hikes, urged caution on the pace of further moves. One known dissenter does not set BoJ policy, but it makes the 'yen +6' scenario even less likely. With Fed officials still pushing for tighter policy, this pair holds its +5 central read.
